<div class="wv-epigraph">{{spoiler|book=cradle-10-reaper|“Ozmanthus Arelius, the original Patriarch of our clan, was known as the greatest Soulsmith of his day,”}}<div class="wv-epigraph-cite">{{spoiler|book=cradle-10-reaper|— ''Reaper'', chapter 10}}</div></div>
{{spoiler|book=cradle-10-reaper|'''Identity:''' later revealed to be [[Eithan]], who he became in the present day.}}

''See also: [[Ozmanthus Arelius Timeline]]''

== Overview ==
{{spoiler|book=cradle-13-threshold|Ozmanthus [[Arelius family|Arelius]] was the founding patriarch of [[Arelius family|House Arelius]] and a legendary figure celebrated as one of history's most talented [[Soulsmiths]]. A genius from his youth, he spent his early years exploring mountain tunnels and searching for Arelia. He achieved significant fame during his time at [[Iron]], where he successfully designed and perfected a custom [[Iron body]]. His mastery of the [[sacred arts]] extended to refining, and he dedicated much of his life to studying ancient [[Soulsmiths]] to establish a lasting legacy for his descendants. Beyond his craftsmanship, he achieved a monumental feat by manifesting an absolute aspect of reality, becoming the Judge of Destruction. Some accounts even refer to him as an interdimensional god of death. Throughout his life, Ozmanthus was characterized by a profound sense of solitude and an intense desire to find intellectual peers who could match his capabilities. Even after ascending to the heavens, he reportedly found himself without equals. In various forms or echoes, such as those found within a [[labyrinth]] or through his [[Soulsmith inheritance]], he appears with a mocking yet elegant demeanor, often carrying a broom and possessing the classic good looks of his bloodline. He is known for his immense [[spiritual perception]], his ability to dismantle techniques, and his command over the [[Arelius bloodline power]]. While he could be arrogant and dismissive, he also expressed a desire to guide others and hoped for the success of those who inherited his knowledge.}}

== History ==
=== {{spoiler|book=cradle-10-reaper|Patriarch of House Arelius}} ===
{{spoiler|book=cradle-10-reaper|While watching falling ash, Ozmanthus [[Arelius family|Arelius]] experienced a sense of personal failure.<ref name="cradle-10-reaper-c1">''Reaper'', chapter 1</ref> A renowned [[Soulsmith]] and the [[original Patriarch]] of the [[Arelius family|Arelius clan]], he named his [[House]] after the city of Arelia.<ref name="cradle-10-reaper-c3">''Reaper'', chapter 3</ref><ref name="cradle-10-reaper-c10">''Reaper'', chapter 10</ref><ref name="cradle-10-reaper-c14">''Reaper'', chapter 14</ref> Ozmanthus perfected his own [[Iron body]] and chose a [[Path]] of [[pure destruction]], eventually manifesting the [[Death Icon]] after engineering a device to kill and revive himself.<ref name="cradle-10-reaper-c3" /> Upon advancing to [[Monarch]], he developed a bloodline ability to see his progress and demonstrated maximum potential in six of the seven [[Abidan]] Divisions.<ref name="cradle-10-reaper-c3" /><ref name="cradle-10-reaper-c10" /> He was capable of inheriting the Mantle of any Judge aside from [[Judge Suriel|Suriel]] and utilized [[soulfire]] along with a black hammer.<ref name="cradle-10-reaper-c10" /><ref name="cradle-10-reaper-c14" /> In his pursuit of perfection, he attempted to create the weapon [[Penance]] and was known for dismantling techniques.<ref name="cradle-10-reaper-c14" /><ref name="cradle-10-reaper-c23">''Reaper'', chapter 23</ref> He left behind a [[Soulsmith inheritance]] and can appear as a black-and-white version of himself or as a projection.<ref name="cradle-10-reaper-c21">''Reaper'', chapter 21</ref><ref name="cradle-10-reaper-c22">''Reaper'', chapter 22</ref>}}

=== {{spoiler|book=cradle-11-dreadgod|Echoes in the Labyrinth}} ===
{{spoiler|book=cradle-11-dreadgod|Ozmanthus [[Arelius family|Arelius]] maintained various workshops and foundries within [[labyrinth|the labyrinth]], some of which remained unplundered.<ref name="cradle-11-dreadgod-c2">''Dreadgod'', chapter 2</ref><ref name="cradle-11-dreadgod-c3">''Dreadgod'', chapter 3</ref> A gray-white ghost appearing as an echo of Ozmanthus was seen using a broom.<ref name="cradle-11-dreadgod-c2" /> This echo provided [[Lindon]] with direction and is revealed to be the same person as [[Eithan|Eithan Arelius]].<ref name="cradle-11-dreadgod-c3" /> Possessing a natural sense for the manipulation of [[madra]], Ozmanthus eventually ascended into the heavens.<ref name="cradle-11-dreadgod-c3" /><ref name="cradle-11-dreadgod-c4">''Dreadgod'', chapter 4</ref> He is also considered a figure who may have provided explanations to the children.<ref name="cradle-11-dreadgod-c11">''Dreadgod'', chapter 11</ref>}}

=== {{spoiler|book=cradle-12-waybound|Master of Yerin}} ===
{{spoiler|book=cradle-12-waybound|Ozmanthus [[Arelius family|Arelius]] serves as the master to [[Yerin]] and is linked to techniques capable of altering a user.<ref name="cradle-12-waybound-c18">''Waybound'', chapter 18</ref><ref name="cradle-12-waybound-c20">''Waybound'', chapter 20</ref> Through memories, [[Dross]] transmits the lethal will of Ozmanthus to [[Yerin]].<ref name="cradle-12-waybound-c20" /> [[Eithan]] considers Ozmanthus when making his decisions and views the man as a figure of pride.<ref name="cradle-12-waybound-c22">''Waybound'', chapter 22</ref><ref name="cradle-12-waybound-c37">''Waybound'', chapter 37</ref> The [[Soulsmith inheritance]] of Ozmanthus was absorbed by [[Reigan Shen|Reigan]], an inheritance that currently taunts the [[Remnant]].<ref name="cradle-12-waybound-c22" /><ref name="cradle-12-waybound-c33">''Waybound'', chapter 33</ref> Having proven that one could return, Ozmanthus once advised the young [[Void Sage]] to utilize the perceptions of others as a looking-glass.<ref name="cradle-12-waybound-c29">''Waybound'', chapter 29</ref><ref name="cradle-12-waybound-c30">''Waybound'', chapter 30</ref>}}
